claim: PF2: one 78 g pellet charge runs 19 min, but melting it takes about 30 min or more, so the die runs at most about 32% of the time
law: Pellet bulk density about 550 kg/m3 (assumed); conduction time ~ r2 / alpha, alpha = k / (rho cp) with k 0.2 W/m K (NETZSCH 0.17 to 0.25), rho 900, cp 1.8; 10 min to reload
check: A pellet bed conducts worse than solid PP and needs latent heat, so the duty is an upper value (independent review 2026-11-12: X1 weak, voids added)

claim: PF2: a 30 mm ram at 1 MPa needs 707 N and 0.62 N m at a 5 mm lead ball screw
law: F = p A; T = F l / (2 pi eta), eta 0.9; NEMA 23 with 10:1 gearbox gives several N m

claim: PF2: a pellet charge melts without trapped air
law: Pellet beds are about 35 to 40 % voids (assumed)
check: Air must be pressed out before the die sees melt, or fibres break; needs a vented compaction stroke

claim: PF2: melt held about 50 min at 250 C stays processable
law: Borealis: degradation rises with temperature and time
check: Ten times the PF1 residence time; MFR drift to measure

claim: PF2: power fits 15 A with the same die width
law: Same air system; the ram barrel heaters replace the extruder heaters
check: Same die width limit (S1); no gain in output

claim: PF3: a heated 150 mm ring at 3500 rpm (27.5 m/s, 10,075 m/s2 at the rim) spins PP into fibres of a few micrometres
law: Molina et al. 2022 (PLOS ONE): 15 cm x 4.5 cm aluminium ring at 3,500 rpm, 160 to 200 C, 8 to 24 holes of 0.41 to 0.97 mm, 24 to 26 g in about 2 min; mean fibre 3.4 to 5.2 um across MFR 12 to 1,550, wide spread (SD 3.0 to 5.2 um)
check: PF3 now uses the demonstrated 150 mm ring (independent review 2026-11-12: X6 refuted, a 60 mm cup gave 2.5 times less rim acceleration; fixed)
closed_by: Option model changed to the 150 mm ring

claim: PF3: power is about 690 to 790 W, well inside 1,440 W
law: Ring heater 450 to 550 W (melt 128 W plus convection from the spinning ring), motor 150 W, controls and corona (estimates)

claim: PF3: the web filters comparably to melt-blown media
law: Molina et al. 2022: best 3-ply web 94.5 % at 16.3 cm H2O against a reference respirator's 97.3 % at 3.7 cm H2O (room-air and incense particles, not NaCl); quality factor -ln(1 - E) / dp
check: Quality factor 0.0018 against 0.0100 per Pa: 5.5 times worse, not comparable (independent review 2026-11-12: should fail). Finer, more even fibres (higher speed, a different ring) might close it but are not demonstrated. Option not carried
closed_by: Noted in OPF-OPT-001; option not carried

claim: PF3: a burst of the spinning ring is contained
law: Kinetic energy 0.5 m r2 w2 for a 0.3 kg ring at 75 mm and 3500 rpm: 113 J
check: Containment by the steel cage rings and a 6 mm polycarbonate enclosure is to assess; no containment criterion was found to cite

claim: PF3: the cage gives an even web
law: Radial throw onto a 500 mm cage; Molina used a drum at -5 kV
check: Deposit is densest at the ring height; a rotating or traversing collector needed; uniformity to measure

claim: PF3: the pellet or flake charge is batch
law: Molina et al. 2022: about 25 g per 2 min run
check: Continuous feed would need a melt feeder into the spinning ring (a different machine)

claim: PF1 on a second 20 A circuit for the air heater: slot up to about 132 mm
law: Air heater at 95 % of 1,920 W on its own circuit; rest on 15 A
check: Needs about 1,800 W of heater (two heaters: the largest 120 V AHPF is 1,200 W), about 2.2 times the air (two pumps) and two supply cords, which raises NFPA 79 disconnect questions (independent review 2026-11-12: X12 weak, hardware not scaled)
